title: Temperature alignment of successive moth composition changes was clear only in early England in four British samples from 1992 to 2015
abstract: We tested whether successive moth composition changes followed a consistent temperature direction. We used 401 three-year trap-month records in England and Scotland in 1992-2003 and 2004-2015. A factorial-moment correction removed shared-middle-catch bias under independent multinomial sampling. The temperature-change product slope was +0.423 in early England, with a four-test interval from +0.300 to +0.545. The other three main intervals included zero. Early English estimates stayed positive after each source-year or trap omission. Thus the positive link did not repeat clearly across countries and periods. Coarse weather, selected complete catches, species-specific capture and few annual clusters limit inference. The result does not identify a causal climate effect. Code, aggregate model evidence, source hashes and external-data retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Successive composition-change alignment slopes and shared-middle-catch correction slopes in four British samples. Bars show approximate four-test intervals.
